issuing_body: BMJ Rapid Recommendations international guideline panel

treatments.name: SGLT-2 inhibitors
treatments.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, stratified by cardiovascular and kidney risk
treatments.summary: Recommended for adults at moderate (weak) or higher (strong) cardiovascular/kidney risk; weak recommendation against for lower-risk adults.

evidence.quote: Lower risk (three or fewer cardiovascular risk factors without established cardiovascular disease (CVD) or chronic kidney disease (CKD)): weak recommendation against SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists.
evidence.statement: For lower-risk adults the panel suggests not using SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists.

evidence.quote: Moderate risk (more than three cardiovascular risk factors without established CVD or CKD; or established CVD and/or CKD at lower risk of complications): weak recommendation in favour of SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists
evidence.statement: For moderate-risk adults the panel suggests using SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists.

evidence.quote: Higher risk (established CVD and/or CKD at higher risk of complications, or established heart failure): strong recommendation in favour of SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists
evidence.statement: For higher-risk adults, including those with heart failure, the panel recommends SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists.

treatments.name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
treatments.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, stratified by cardiovascular and kidney risk
treatments.summary: Same risk-stratified recommendations as SGLT-2 inhibitors: against at lower risk, in favour at moderate and higher risk.

evidence.quote: Lower risk (three or fewer cardiovascular risk factors without established cardiovascular disease (CVD) or chronic kidney disease (CKD)): weak recommendation against SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists.
evidence.statement: For lower-risk adults the panel suggests not using SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists.

evidence.quote: Moderate risk (more than three cardiovascular risk factors without established CVD or CKD; or established CVD and/or CKD at lower risk of complications): weak recommendation in favour of SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists
evidence.statement: For moderate-risk adults the panel suggests using SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists.

evidence.quote: Higher risk (established CVD and/or CKD at higher risk of complications, or established heart failure): strong recommendation in favour of SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists
evidence.statement: For higher-risk adults, including those with heart failure, the panel recommends SGLT-2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists.

treatments.name: Finerenone
treatments.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease
treatments.summary: Weak recommendation against at moderate risk and weak recommendation in favour at higher risk of complications.

evidence.quote: and a weak recommendation against finerenone in adults with CKD
evidence.statement: For moderate-risk adults with CKD the panel suggests not using finerenone.

evidence.quote: and a weak recommendation in favour of finerenone in adults with CKD
evidence.statement: For higher-risk adults with CKD the panel suggests using finerenone.

treatments.name: Tirzepatide
treatments.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity, across risk strata
treatments.summary: Weak recommendation in favour of tirzepatide for adults with obesity regardless of cardiovascular or kidney risk.

evidence.quote: Across risk strata: weak recommendation in favour of tirzepatide in adults with obesity.
evidence.statement: The panel suggests tirzepatide for adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity.

milestones.label: Living evidence review underpinning the tirzepatide recommendation updated
milestones.quote: network meta-analysis evaluating relative benefits and harms updated to 31 July 2024

notes: Living guideline; recommendations are stratified by cardiovascular and kidney risk rather than by line of therapy.
